newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-National's Boswell sees GST on second term agenda.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-National's Boswell sees GST on second term agenda.

text.p: Australia's National Party senate Leader Ron Boswell said on Sunday his party, which forms the Coalition government with the Liberal party, would want to put a Goods and Services Tax (GST) on the agenda for its second term.

"I think the party does want to move into a consumption tax or a GST, but the Coalition and the leadership of the Coalition are very nervous about it," Boswell told Channel Ten's Meet The Press programme.
"There's a lot in it for the bush. They would be the major beneficiaries with the removal of the diesel excise," Boswell said.
"I think the National party will want it on the agenda for the second term, but we don't want to frighten the horses," Boswell said.
"We've been bitten with it once and we don't want to go and get bitten on the other hand."
The Coalition lost the 1993 election after it campaigned for a GST. It went to the March 2, 1996 election saying it did not plan a GST.
Since then the government has been careful to say it did not plan a GST in its first three year term which ends in 1999.
Responding to Boswell's comments, Prime Minister John Howard again said he was opposed to a GST in the current term.
"There won't be a GST in this parliament (term). I said that and there has been no change," Howard told reporters in country Victoria.
But he would not speculate on what might happen after 1999.
"I have only just got there. You ask me about the next parliament when we are coming towards it," he said.
"Heavens above, I am only just settling in."
